candidates.decision_relevance: Would show whether participation weakened or recovered before, during, and after the price moves, helping distinguish persistent broad deterioration from proxy or endpoint effects.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews repeatedly cite point-in-time Top-100 breadth proxies with changing membership; canonical broad-alt and large-cap breadth are unconfirmed. W41 also lacks quantitative breadth sequences.
candidates.metric_name: Fixed-universe asset breadth with constituent membership and timestamps
candidates.missing_history_problem: Comparable historical breadth values and their point-in-time universe membership are missing, so persistence and sequencing cannot be assessed.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would help establish whether spot participation and liquidity conditions deteriorated before or after price weakness, rather than relying on brief, mixed snapshots.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews describe short spot microstructure snapshots and incomplete, lower-bound liquidation captures; weekly reviews identify missing spot-participation and liquidity sequences.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped BTC and ETH spot participation and depth observations
candidates.missing_history_problem: Prior observations on a consistent sampling basis are absent or too sparse to evaluate persistence and lead-lag relative to price.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would clarify whether mixed BTC and ETH flows persisted, reversed, or changed alongside relative performance and breadth.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews repeatedly report settled ETF rows only through October 9, while weekly reviews cite mixed or negative totals without a complete within-period sequence.
candidates.metric_name: Daily settled BTC and ETH ETF flow sequence
candidates.missing_history_problem: Intervening settled sessions and a longer comparable history are not supplied, preventing assessment of flow persistence and timing.
